C32.content_en:
Ways to see who searches a keyword by age and gender — and how the main tools compare

If you write a blog, you want to know whether your likely readers lean toward an age group or a gender before you start. Enter one keyword and this tool shows the age and gender tendencies of people who search it, in two tables.

Method / toolPricing modelNotes
This tool (DataForSEO)Pay per request. About $0.0024 per call (measured)An age table and a gender table. Values are relative, with the top group set to 100. Save as CSV
SimilarWebSubscription (its pricing page lists a Starter plan from $125/month)Profiles the people who visit a site (age, gender and more). Estimates of site visitors, not of keyword searchers
Google AnalyticsFreeShows the profile of your own site's visitors. Needs a site of your own
Social ad managersAvailable in ad setup screens (check each vendor's official site for conditions)Shows audience size by age and gender for ad targeting

Checked in November 2026. Prices change — confirm on each vendor's official site before you buy.

Why use this tool

  • Tendencies of people who search a keyword. No site of your own needed.
  • About $0.0024. About 400 per $1, so you can check each post idea.
  • About 1 second.
  • Works for the US and other countries. "side hustle" in the US returned age and gender (measured). A test with "副業" in Japan also worked.
  • Save as CSV.

When it is not the right fit

  • You want percentages → the values are relative to the largest group (set to 100); they do not add up to 100%.
  • You want people aged 55 and over → the age groups are 18-24, 25-34, 35-44 and 45-54. Older groups are not returned (measured).
  • You want head counts → this tool cannot show them.
  • You want the profile of site visitors → this is about people who search the keyword. For site visitors, SimilarWeb and similar tools fit better.

This tool does one thing: show the age and gender tendencies of people who search a keyword.

FAQ

What do the numbers mean?

They are relative to the largest group, which is 100. For "side hustle" in the US, 25-34 was 100, 18-24 was 96, female was 100 and male was 79.

Why is there no 55+ group?

The API returns four groups: 18-24, 25-34, 35-44 and 45-54.

Why is there no language selector?

This API accepts a country only.

Does every keyword work?

Rarely searched words may return no numbers. Then the table is empty.

Can I sign up with a free email address?

No. DataForSEO does not accept free email providers. See What is DataForSEO?

C33.content_en:
Ways to see which countries search a keyword — and how the main tools compare

If you publish for people overseas, you want to know which countries search a word most first. Enter one keyword and this tool returns search volume and share per country as a table.

Method / toolPricing modelNotes
This tool (DataForSEO)Pay per request. About $0.18 per call (measured: $0.18 for one keyword, and also $0.18 for 2)Volume and share per country in a table. Save as CSV. Countries come as ISO codes (US, IN, DE and so on)
Ahrefs Keywords ExplorerSubscription (see the official site for plans)Shows global volume with a country breakdown
Google Keyword Planner (by hand)Free (needs a Google Ads account)You pick a country to research (see the official site for features)
Semrush Keyword OverviewSubscription (see the official site)Switch countries to see a keyword overview

Checked in November 2026. Prices change — confirm on each vendor's official site before you buy.

Why use this tool

  • The breakdown by country in one call. "ramen" returned 139 countries (measured; the United States about 18%, India about 9%). A Japanese-language keyword returned only 52 countries in a separate test (measured in Japan with a Japanese keyword; Japan about 96%).
  • Share included. See at once how lopsided it is.
  • A few seconds. We measured about 0.1 seconds for the US sample.
  • Other languages work too. The number of countries depends on the word.
  • Save as CSV.

When it is not the right fit

  • You want to test many ideas cheaply → at $0.18 per call the price is on the high side.
  • You want country names → countries stay as ISO codes (US, IN and so on). We do not convert them.
  • You want states or cities within a country → this is country level only.
  • The numbers are the API's estimates of search volume.
  • You want only the top countries → every returned country is shown: 139 for "ramen" in our US sample.
  • Each call fetches one keyword; there is no country or language setting.

This tool does one thing: show a keyword's search volume and share by country.

FAQ

Why is it $0.18?

That is the API's price per call. Sending 2 keywords to the API also cost $0.18, and so did a single keyword.

What are the country codes?

US is the United States and IN is India, as two-letter ISO codes.

Why is there no country or language selector?

The numbers cover all countries worldwide.

What is the share a share of?

Each country's part of the total of the returned countries (US 80,109 ÷ total 437,044 = 18.33%, checked for "ramen").

Can I sign up with a free email address?

No. DataForSEO does not accept free email providers. See What is DataForSEO?
